mdmp.title: The seven MDMP steps and their key outputs
mdmp.caption: The seven MDMP steps. The outputs of one step become the inputs of the next; warning orders go out after Steps 1, 2 and 6.

steps.label: Receipt of mission
steps.note: Commander's initial guidance

steps.label: Mission analysis
steps.note: The most critical step: problem statement, mission statement, initial intent and planning guidance, initial CCIRs and EEFIs, COA evaluation criteria

steps.label: COA development
steps.note: Screen each COA: feasible, acceptable, suitable, distinguishable, complete. S3 prepares the COA statement and sketch

steps.label: COA analysis (war game)
steps.note: Action, reaction, counteraction. Belt, avenue-in-depth or box method; no comparing COAs

steps.label: COA comparison
steps.note: Weigh COAs against criteria fixed beforehand; lowest decision-matrix total is most desirable

steps.label: COA approval
steps.note: Commander approves, modifies or rejects; final planning guidance

steps.label: Orders production, dissemination and transition
steps.note: COA statement becomes the concept of operations; S6 prepares Annex H (Signal)

steps.label: Issue a warning order
steps.note: Enough known information for subordinates to start preparing

steps.label: Initiate movement

steps.label: Complete the plan

steps.label: Issue the order

steps.label: Supervise and refine

signalplanning.title: The signal planning process
signalplanning.caption: Signal planning runs alongside MDMP, or TLP at small-unit level: requirements, real capability, priorities, tentative plan, final checks, publication.

steps.label: Develop requirements
steps.note: Commander's priorities, staff and unit coordination, SOPs, applicable CEOI and CESI

steps.label: Check real capability
steps.note: Equipment readiness, actual personnel fill, training and funds

steps.label: Set priorities
steps.note: When resources are short, rank by supportability and importance to the mission

steps.label: Prepare for disruptions
steps.note: Redundant service, repair or replacement, technical support

steps.label: Prepare the tentative plan
steps.note: Allocate resources; primary, alternate, contingency and emergency support

steps.label: Final checks, then publish
steps.note: Coverage, responsibilities, resources, security, priorities; publish diagrams and instructions with the plans and orders

cyberrisk.title: From asset to mission risk
cyberrisk.caption: Asset means value, threat means potential harm, and vulnerability means exploitable weakness. Likelihood and mission consequence complete the risk statement.

steps.label: Asset
steps.note: Name it and the confidentiality, integrity or availability it needs

steps.label: Threat
steps.note: Something that could affect the asset

steps.label: Vulnerability
steps.note: The weakness that lets the threat cause harm

steps.label: Likelihood
steps.note: Explain how likely the harm is

steps.label: Mission consequence
steps.note: Explain what the harm means for the mission

steps.label: Preparation
steps.note: Readies people, tools and procedures

steps.label: Identification

steps.label: Containment

ethicalleadership.topic: Six steps for an ethical decision
ethicalleadership.title: Six steps for an ethical decision
ethicalleadership.caption: Define, know the rules, develop options, evaluate, decide and act, reflect. Compare alternatives explicitly before acting.

steps.label: Define the dilemma
steps.note: Identify the duties or values in tension

steps.label: Know the rules
steps.note: Laws, orders, regulations and values that apply

steps.label: Develop options
steps.note: Generate feasible courses of action

steps.label: Evaluate
steps.note: Test each for legal, moral and mission implications

steps.label: Decide and act
steps.note: Take responsibility for the action

steps.label: Reflect
steps.note: Learn from the outcome and prevent recurrence

datacomms.title: Sizing voice on a link: the worked example
datacomms.caption: Brigade TOC to division over VSAT: 15 compressed calls plus 400 kbps of data, with a margin of at least 25 percent.

steps.label: Voice
steps.note: 15 calls × about 30 kbps = 450 kbps

steps.label: Add the data
steps.note: 450 + 400 kbps = 850 kbps

steps.label: Add the margin
steps.note: 850 × 1.25 ≈ 1,060 kbps for peaks and overhead

steps.label: Plan the link
steps.note: Roughly 1.1 Mbps or more, or reduce calls, or move bulk data off the link at peak hours
